findings.case: safeDecrypt's warn logs `looksWellFormed: isEncrypted(value)`, but that branch is only reachable when isEncrypted(value)===true (guard at :388) — the field is always true. findings.fix: Drop the field, or log a real shape signal (v2 prefix present + parseable 3-segment body). One line.

findings.case: parseDsl validates operator/value for the 8 simple operators but accepts the two windowed operators (count_in_last_N_minutes / distinct_count_in_last_N_hours) with ANY value shape. A rule saved as {field:'event.ip', operator:'count_in_last_N_minutes', value:5} passes parse, is stored, and then silently evaluates to 'unknown' on every scoring pass (evalClause requires value.n to be a number) — the rule never fires and nothing ever reports why.
findings.fix: In parseDsl, for the two windowed operators require typeof cl.value==='object' && Number.isFinite(cl.value.n) and reject otherwise (~3 lines, same error shape as the other clause checks).

findings.case: All four Redis ops (isAlertingPaused get, pauseAlerting set, resumeAlerting del, tryClaimAlertDedupe set-NX-EX) are raw client calls with no withRedisCommandTimeout wrapper — every other Redis consumer on this tree (account-link-consent, scheduler-coordinator) bounds its commands after the r103 gray-zone incident (client isReady but socket black-holed). In that gray zone the scheduled forecast run hangs on the flag read until the socket errors out — the try/catch here catches errors, not hangs, so the pipeline stalls instead of degrading.
findings.fix: Wrap the ops with withRedisCommandTimeout like account-link-consent.ts:198-210 (catch -> same warn + degraded fallback: false / true / no-op).

notes: Degrade posture (emit-when-down on dedupe, assume-not-paused on read) is documented and reasonable; NX on pause keeps manual-clear semantics. Only the unbounded-command gap above.

findings.case: exchangeFirebaseIdToken and refreshFirebaseSession use raw fetch with no timeout and an unguarded res.json(). A stalled backend hangs the Google sign-in flow until the browser's ~300s TCP timeout — the exact class R142 D-3 just fixed for the admin surface (adminFetch's 20s DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS). A non-JSON 502 body (proxy HTML) throws an English SyntaxError ('Unexpected token <') straight into the Arabic error-toast path. The token-refresh listener's circuit breaker limits frequency, not duration.
findings.fix: Reuse the app timeout contract (AbortSignal.timeout(DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)) and parse via res.json().catch(() => null) with a fallback error, mirroring adminFetchJson's shape.
